title: Soy-Garlic Grilled Shrimp
shortDescription: Large shrimp in a quick soy-garlic, honey, rice-vinegar, ginger, scallion, and sesame marinade, grilled until pearly and opaque.
culturalContext: Soy, garlic, scallion, ginger, and sesame form a familiar Korean seasoning family. Applying that profile to skewered grilled shrimp is presented here as a contemporary home-grilling adaptation rather than a singular traditional formula.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Clean cutting board and paring knife
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill

ingredients.item: raw large shrimp, about 16–20 count per pound
ingredients.preparation: refrigerator-thawed if frozen, peeled and deveined; tails optional

mixOrder: Whisk soy sauce, honey, vinegar, sesame oil, and pepper.
Stir in garlic, ginger, and scallions.
Reserve 60 ml / 1/4 cup in a clean bowl before raw shrimp contact.
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 30 minutes; soy and vinegar can make shrimp overly salty and alter the surface texture.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Move 60 ml / 1/4 cup to a clean finishing bowl before adding raw shrimp.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard marinade and brushes that contacted raw shrimp; finish only with the untouched reserved sauce.
substitutions: Certified gluten-free tamari may replace soy sauce after label review.
Maple syrup may replace honey by volume, changing flavor and browning.
allergenNotes: Regular soy sauce usually contains wheat.

instructions.heading: Prepare dry shrimp
instructions.action: Thaw in the refrigerator, peel, and devein with clean tools. Do not rinse; pat each shrimp very dry.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Shrimp are firm, dry, and mild-smelling without translucent ice glaze.
instructions.safetyNote: Reject leaking packages or shrimp with sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia-like odor; sanitize the prep area.

instructions.heading: Mix and reserve sauce
instructions.action: Whisk soy sauce, honey, vinegar, sesame oil, and pepper; stir in garlic, ginger, and scallions. Reserve 60 ml / 1/4 cup in a clean bowl.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Honey is dissolved and aromatics are evenly dispersed.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the reserved finishing sauce and its brush completely away from raw seafood.

instructions.heading: Marinate and skewer
instructions.action: Coat shrimp for 10 to 15 minutes under refrigeration, then thread through two points on metal skewers.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Shrimp lie flat and carry a thin coating rather than dripping sauce.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard all raw-contact marinade; never leave shrimp marinating at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Prepare the grill surface
instructions.action: Preheat the approved grill to medium-high, clean it, and oil it lightly. Arrange a clean cooked-food platter and utensils.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Shrimp sizzle promptly and the first side releases after setting.
instructions.safetyNote: Use only approved indoor electric equipment indoors and follow manufacturer ventilation and grease directions.

instructions.heading: Grill to full opacity
instructions.action: Grill 2 to 3 minutes on the first side and 1 to 3 minutes on the second, checking the center of the thickest shrimp.
instructions.temperature: Official cue: pearly or white and opaque throughout
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: No translucent band remains and the flesh is pearly and firm.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not rely only on pink exterior color or curl; inspect the thickest center.

instructions.heading: Finish cleanly
instructions.action: Transfer to the clean platter and brush lightly with untouched reserved sauce using a clean brush.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Shrimp are glossy without pooled sauce.
instructions.safetyNote: Never reuse the raw-seafood brush, bowl, or marinade on cooked shrimp.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high. Follow the appliance manual for ventilation, clearances, grease handling, and grate care; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: FoodSafety.gov lists no numeric minimum for shrimp; cook until flesh is pearly or white and opaque throughout.
visualDonenessCues: No translucent center remains in the thickest shrimp.
Flesh is pearly or white, opaque, and firm without becoming hard.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep seafood at 40°F / 4°C or below and thaw in the refrigerator, not on the counter.
Do not rinse raw seafood; splashing can spread contamination. Peel, devein, or remove side muscles with clean tools, then pat dry.
Use separate raw and cooked plates, tongs, brushes, and skewers, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
FoodSafety.gov directs cooking shrimp and scallops until the flesh is pearly or white and opaque; time alone is not a doneness test.
Pregnant, immunocompromised, older, and very young diners should not be served raw or undercooked seafood.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: Use comparably sized shrimp to keep cooking times consistent.
Certified gluten-free tamari addresses only the soy-sauce ingredient; labels and cross-contact still require review.
ingredientSourcing: Choose firm mild-smelling shrimp or intact frozen packages without heavy frost or evidence of refreezing.
Check soy sauce and sesame oil labels for declared allergens and cross-contact.
makeAhead: Mix and refrigerate the sauce up to 1 day ahead. Thaw shrimp in the refrigerator and marinate only 10 to 15 minutes shortly before grilling.
storage: Refrigerate cooked shrimp within 2 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below and use within 2 days.
reheating: Reheat to 165°F / 74°C with brief gentle heat; discard leftovers that have been repeatedly warmed or held out too long.
leftovers: Use reheated shrimp in rice bowls or chopped lettuce wraps with fresh garnishes added afterward.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice and a crisp fresh or lightly pickled vegetable.
Use individual sauce dishes and keep raw seafood away from communal banchan.

faq.question: Can shrimp marinate overnight?
faq.answer: No. This salty, acidic sauce is designed for 10 to 15 minutes and should not exceed 30 minutes.

faq.question: Do I need to rinse peeled shrimp?
faq.answer: No. FoodSafety.gov advises not rinsing raw seafood because splashing spreads contamination; peel, devein, and pat dry instead.

metaDescription: Make soy-garlic grilled shrimp with a brief refrigerated marinade, clean finishing sauce, anti-sticking preparation, and opaque-doneness cues.
sourcesAndEditorialNotes: Seasoning-family comparison: https://www.maangchi.com/recipe/bulgogi (soy, garlic, ginger, scallion, and sesame proportions used only as comparative context).
Contemporary shrimp formulation created for the locked title; no canonical-history or test-cooked claim is made.

buyingCues: Firm shrimp with a mild odor and no sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia-like smell.
Frozen packages are intact without large ice crystals, freezer burn, or signs of thawing and refreezing.
seafoodPreparation.thawing: Thaw in a covered container overnight in the refrigerator. For a faster method, keep sealed under cold water, changing water every 30 minutes, then cook immediately.
seafoodPreparation.cleaningOrShellPreparation: Peel and devein with clean tools; tails are optional. Do not rinse raw shrimp.
seafoodPreparation.drying: Pat thoroughly dry with disposable towels before marinating.
seafoodPreparation.scoringOrSkewering: Thread through two points on metal skewers to prevent spinning.
seafoodPreparation.grillSurfacePreparation: Preheat, clean, and lightly oil the grill surface.
seafoodPreparation.stickingPrevention: Dry well, oil the surface lightly, and wait for the first side to set and release before turning.
seafoodPreparation.approximateTime: About 4 to 6 minutes total for large shrimp.
donenessCues: Pearly or white and opaque throughout.
seafoodPreparation.applicableTemperature: FoodSafety.gov provides the visual standard pearly or white and opaque rather than a numeric shrimp minimum.
seafoodPreparation.shellOpeningAndDiscardGuidance: Not applicable to peeled shrimp; discard shells promptly and sanitize tools and surfaces.
crossContactNotes: Keep raw marinade, skewers, brush, and tongs separate from the clean cooked-food set.
Reserve finishing sauce before raw contact and discard all contaminated sauce.
